narrative:
The 2025 Milwaukee Brewers arrived as a club with genuine aspirations, and the early weeks of the season immediately illustrated both their ceiling and their vulnerability. Closer Trevor Megill emerged as an unlikely villain in his own team's story, surrendering critical late-game runs in April that cost Milwaukee wins they desperately needed. Yet the young core refused to blink — Jackson Chourio's bat came alive with a towering two-run blast on April 26, and Caleb Durbin announced himself as a clutch performer in May, delivering a walk-off single that kept the Brewers afloat through a turbulent spring.

The summer months brought turbulence from an unexpected source: Abner Uribe, entrusted with high-leverage relief innings, was torched repeatedly in May and July. Oneil Cruz and Brady House both victimized him with crushing home runs, threatening to destabilize a pitching staff that was otherwise one of baseball's elite units. But Milwaukee's lineup answered every challenge. Andrew Vaughn proved to be the team's most clutch performer, delivering a go-ahead single in July and following it with a piercing double that turned the tide in a critical series. William Contreras elevated his game to another level entirely, launching back-to-back massive home runs in mid-to-late August — including a stunning two-run shot on August 17 that carried a WPA of 0.644, the single most impactful positive play of the entire regular season.

The Brewers ground out the final stretch with characteristic grit, overcoming late-season stumbles including a brutal Heliot Ramos single off Megill on August 24 that wiped out a lead, and a momentum-killing double play off Jackson Chourio's bat in September. Jared Koenig's clutch twin killing in the penultimate week of September helped seal a remarkable 97-win season. Built on a 3.58 ERA and 806 runs scored, Milwaukee won the NL Central and earned home-field advantage into October, entering the playoffs as one of baseball's most complete teams.

The postseason opened with fireworks in the Division Series against the Cubs. Andrew Vaughn launched a three-run homer and Jackson Chourio added his own three-run blast in Game 1, and Milwaukee dispatched Chicago in what felt like a coming-out party for this franchise. But the Championship Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers proved a bridge too far. Aaron Ashby surrendered a three-run Seiya Suzuki homer in the NLDS, and Freddy Peralta was tagged for a three-run Ian Happ shot in a pivotal Game 2. The NLCS provided fleeting hope — a Quinn Priester double play and a Jake Bauers ground-rule double had Milwaukee threatening in Game 1 — but Brice Turang's swinging strikeout in a crucial moment deflated a potential rally, and Tommy Edman's single off Jacob Misiorowski in Game 4 proved the death blow. The Brewers fell in the NLCS, a heartbreaking end to one of the most accomplished seasons in franchise history.

chapters.title: Shaky Start, Stubborn Heart
chapters.description: Trevor Megill's early meltdowns threaten to derail Milwaukee's season before young hitters like Chourio and Durbin fight back.

chapters.title: Uribe Under Fire
chapters.description: Abner Uribe is hammered in high-leverage situations across a brutal stretch in May and July, testing the Brewers' bullpen depth.

chapters.title: Vaughn Steps Up
chapters.description: Andrew Vaughn emerges as Milwaukee's clutch catalyst, delivering back-to-back pivotal hits in July to stabilize a team fighting for first place.

chapters.title: Contreras Carries the Club
chapters.description: William Contreras puts the team on his back in August with a pair of massive home runs, headlined by the season's highest single-play WPA swing.

chapters.title: Grinding to the Wire
chapters.description: The Brewers survive a brutal late-August implosion and September turbulence to clinch 97 wins and claim their division title.

chapters.title: October Dreams, Dodger Blues
chapters.description: Milwaukee storms past the Cubs in the Division Series behind Vaughn and Chourio home runs, then meets its match against the Dodgers in a heartbreaking NLCS exit.
